paper.title_en: Temperature dependence of energy deposition in the Lead Tungstate calorimeter at MUonE
paper.abstract_en:
The goal of the MUonE experiment is to provide an independent measurement of the leading-order
hadronic vacuum polarisation contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, aHLO
μ .
The method to achieve this is to measure the angular correlation between outgoing muons and elec-
trons scattered from atomic electrons. In the experimental setup is an electromagnetic calorimeter
(ECAL) used to measure the energy of the electrons. To ensure proper functionality and compar-
ison between events, the behaviour of the ECAL must be understood for changes in temperature
that could occur during the data taking. This investigation aims to measure the analogue-to-digital
converter (ADC) counts for 100 GeV electrons incident on each lead tungstate crystal in the ECAL
at 14◦C, 19◦C, 22◦C and 24◦C and determine a calibration function for each ECAL crystal. It was
found that the ADC counts measured in the crystals appear to decrease as a function of tempera-
ture, linearly, and that the rate of change also appears to be subtly different in each crystal. The
negative gradient agrees with pre-established theory however, the calibration functions could not
be confidently determined due to an insufficient number of measured temperatures. Going forward
more measurements should be made at more temperatures for a proper calibration to be produced.
